extDescription.message: Multiple address bar keywords for your search engines – e.g. @w, @wiki and @wikipedia for Wikipedia.

optEnginesHint.message: Enable the search engine that is set as default in Firefox. The add-on spots extra keywords on its result page – it only gets access to that, nothing else.

optFfHint.message: Enter extra keywords on the right, separated by commas. Saved automatically.

newEngineIntro.message: You add new search engines in Firefox itself (add-ons aren't allowed to):

newEngineStep1.message: Open Firefox Settings → Search (if no tab opened: type about:preferences#search into the address bar)

newEngineStep2.message: Under “Search engines” click “Add”: enter name, search URL with %s and the main keyword (e.g. @w)

newEngineStep3.message: Switch back to this tab – the engine appears here automatically

newEngineAfter.message: Then add the extra keywords here.

mainActiveTip.message: Typing $alias$ makes Firefox show “$engine$”. Change it in Firefox Settings → Search.

mainNoneTip.message: This engine has no keyword in Firefox. Extra keywords still work, but a main keyword (Firefox Settings → Search → pencil) adds the name label.

optCustomTitle.message: 3. Exception: targets without a Firefox search engine

optCustomHint.message: Only needed if you don't want to add a target as a Firefox search engine. Target by URL, %s stands for the search terms. No name label while typing.

confirmReset.message: Replace all custom targets with the examples?

statusInvalid.message: Not saved – please check the fields marked red

errFirefoxAlias.message: $alias$ is already the Firefox keyword of “$engine$”

errUrl.message: URL must start with http(s):// and contain %s

guideLead.message: This add-on doesn't replace your Firefox search engines, it extends them: each engine has one main keyword in Firefox, and here you give it as many extra keywords as you like.

guideStep1Title.message: Add the engine in Firefox, with your favourite keyword

guideStep1Text.message: Firefox Settings → Search. Use the keyword you type most often (e.g. @y). Only for that one does Firefox show the engine's name while you type.

guideStep2Text.message: Under “2. Your Firefox search engines”, enter e.g. @yt and @youtube. They lead to the same search – handy as a safety net when you mistype or are used to a different keyword.

guideStep3Text.message: Under “1.” tick the search engine that's your Firefox default. That's how the add-on spots the extra keywords.

guideBarMain.message: Firefox shows “YouTube” right away. You see where you're searching while typing.

guideBarExtra.message: Firefox says “Search with Google”, but after Enter you still land on YouTube.

guideNoteTitle.message: Why doesn't Firefox show the name for extra keywords?

guideNoteText.message: Add-ons aren't allowed to change the address bar. The add-on only steps in after Enter and redirects the search. So: the keyword you use most belongs in Firefox as the main keyword – the extra keywords are the add-on.

guideTipAt.message: Tip: type just @ into the address bar and Firefox lists all engines with their main keywords.

guideTipCustom.message: Exception: under “3.” you can add targets with no Firefox search engine at all, just a URL. None of their keywords get a name label then.
